symptoms: The stage takes far longer than an earlier run over comparable input, then fails
Executor time is dominated by garbage collection rather than by work
Adding heap postpones the failure instead of removing it
likely_causes: The live set nearly fills the heap, so the collector runs constantly and recovers little
Cached data is holding memory the execution side needs
Many small objects per record, which multiplies collection work without multiplying data
diagnostic_steps: Read the share of executor time spent in garbage collection for the failing stage: this error is about the ratio, not about a single allocation
Check what the job caches and whether it is still needed at that point
Read the effective spark.memory.fraction, whose Spark default is 0.6 of heap minus 300MB for execution and storage
fixes: Reduce the live set: drop caches that are no longer read, and narrow the columns carried through the stage
Raise heap when the live set is genuinely large and the collector simply lacks room
Reduce object churn per record where the job builds many short-lived objects
unsafe_fixes: Raising heap without measuring the collection ratio, which buys time and returns as soon as the input grows
Raising spark.memory.fraction, which the Spark documentation recommends leaving at its default and which requires JVM garbage collection tuning alongside
verification: Share of executor time in garbage collection for the same stage, before and after, over the same input volume
rollback: Revert the memory override or restore the cache that was dropped; neither changes data
